item.title: LLM-Guided Quantum Code Discovery
item.description:
An “AI for science” workflow that uses large language models to evolve Python programs generating quantum LDPC code designs: bivariate-bicycle (BB) and perturbed bivariate-bicycle (PBB) codes. Built on OpenEvolve with an ensemble of LLMs, and paired with an independent verification stack so every reported code is certified rather than just proposed.

Results:

  • 465 distinct codes (97 CSS, 368 non-CSS) at block length n ≤ 360, from ~200K candidates screened across five campaigns — about 140 hours and ~US$400 in LLM inference
  • Notable finds include an indecomposable [[288,16,12]] code, higher-rate codes reaching k = 50 at d = 8, and non-CSS codes matching the gross-code benchmark at [[144,12,12]]
  • Follow-up on weight-five codes: a 1,142-entry catalogue with exact distance certificates, structural analysis, and random-search controls

Verification pipeline: GF(2) rank computation, MILP-based distance bounds, BLISS Tanner-graph deduplication, decomposability analysis, and local-Clifford equivalence checks — designed to catch the search’s own blind spots.

Presented as an invited keynote at the AI4QC workshop, IEEE Quantum Week 2026. Code, catalogues, and paper sources are open under Apache 2.0.

item.title: Qiskit Code Assistant
item.description:
A family of LLMs (8B–24B parameters) specialized for quantum code generation. Models built on IBM Granite, Mistral, and Qwen foundations, fine-tuned on curated Qiskit datasets including Python scripts, Jupyter notebooks, and synthetic Q&A pairs.

Open-source model family:

  • Mistral Small 24B — Largest model, highest accuracy
  • Qwen2.5 Coder 14B — Strong coding foundation
  • Granite 3.x 8B — Efficient, multiple versions
  • GGUF quantized versions available for local deployment

across 11 model repositories, including the GGUF versions.

Achieves 46.53% on Qiskit HumanEval—significantly outperforming competing models (24.75%–39.6%). Supports natural language to code (“define a Bell circuit and run it on ibm_brisbane”) and intelligent autocomplete.

Post-training with quantum-verifiable rewards: a synthetic pipeline generates quantum problem–unit test pairs, used for DPO preference data and for GRPO training with rewards checked by execution on quantum systems. The combined DPO + GRPO model beats the strongest open-source baselines on Qiskit HumanEval Hard ( ).

We created and open-sourced Qiskit HumanEval and Qiskit HumanEval Hard—benchmarks with 150+ tasks each, now used industry-wide for evaluating quantum code LLMs. Integrated into VS Code and JupyterLab.

item.title: qiskit-ibm-transpiler
item.description:
AI-powered quantum circuit optimization that outperforms traditional heuristics. Uses reinforcement learning to achieve near-optimal synthesis of Linear Function, Clifford, and Permutation circuits—orders of magnitude faster than SAT solvers. Our Pauli Network synthesis delivers over 2× reduction in two-qubit gate count, with average improvements of 20% and up to 60% on the Benchpress benchmark.

Supports hardware-aware routing up to 133 qubits and works as a drop-in replacement for standard Qiskit transpilation. Available as both local execution (with our open-source RL models) and cloud-based services.

item.title: Qiskit Gym
item.description:
Gymnasium-compatible RL environments for training AI agents to synthesize quantum circuits. The framework that powers the AI transpiler passes achieving state-of-the-art results in qiskit-ibm-transpiler.

Three synthesis environments:

  • Permutation Synthesis — Minimal SWAP gate implementations respecting hardware coupling
  • Linear Function Synthesis — CNOT-optimal decomposition of Boolean linear functions
  • Clifford Synthesis — Hardware-efficient implementations of Clifford group elements

Hardware-aware design matches real quantum device coupling maps. High-performance Rust backend enables fast training. Supports PPO, AlphaZero, and custom policies with built-in TensorBoard visualization.

The agents trained with this framework achieve near-optimal synthesis up to 65 qubits—orders of magnitude faster than SAT solvers.

item.title: Qiskit MCP Servers
item.description:
Production-ready Model Context Protocol servers that give AI assistants direct access to quantum computing infrastructure. Built on FastMCP with async-first architecture, full type safety, and 65%+ test coverage.

Five specialized servers:

  • Qiskit Server — Circuit creation, manipulation, and transpilation
  • Code Assistant Server — AI-assisted quantum programming via Granite models
  • IBM Runtime Server — Hardware access, job execution, and backend selection
  • AI Transpiler Server — RL-powered circuit optimization
  • Qiskit Gym Server — Lets AI agents train RL models for circuit synthesis on their own: create environments, launch PPO or AlphaZero training, and synthesize circuits ( )

Enables AI systems to autonomously generate quantum code, select optimal backends, execute circuits on real hardware, train their own circuit-synthesis models, and provide expert quantum computing guidance—all through a standardized protocol.

item.title: IBM Quantum Job Scheduling
item.description:
Designed and implemented the fair-share queue that decides the order in which jobs run on IBM Quantum hardware. It balances access across users and organizations according to their allocations, and it schedules every job run on every IBM Quantum QPU — still in production today.

Later, as Data & Intelligence Chapter Lead, I led work on predicting QPU processing time for user jobs, which has been deployed on production since 2023. Based on this experience, we published a paper at IEEE QCE 2025 in which we used a dataset of ~150,000 jobs following the IBM Quantum schema, gradient-boosting models (LightGBM) forecast how long each job will take on the hardware, giving scheduling and resource management a better signal than static estimates.

item.title: IBM Quantum Lab
item.description:
Led development of IBM Quantum Lab, the cloud notebook environment where IBM Quantum users wrote and ran Qiskit code against real quantum hardware without installing anything. Built as a JupyterHub deployment on Kubernetes integrated with the IBM Quantum platform, open to ~240,000 enrolled users.

Engineering challenges solved:

  • Custom authentication against the IBM Quantum platform
  • Persistent per-user storage and tailored user environments with Qiskit and tutorials pre-installed
  • Automatic selection of hardware resources for different user profiles
  • Abuse protection and performance at scale — peaks of ~800 concurrent user servers during the IBM Quantum Challenge

Presented at JupyterCon 2020.
